finding.claim: Unsigned tokens (empty signature, alg HS256 or any non-none algorithm) are accepted when the verifier key is an empty string or null, because the missing-key guards only fire when a key or a signature is present.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied token base64url({"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}).base64url({"sub":"admin"}). with an empty signature segment
finding.sink: verifyToken returns the payload as a valid, authenticated token

trace.note: createVerifier accepts keyType 'string' or 'object' without rejecting '' or null; only undefined and non-string/object types throw
Key detection and prepareKeyOrSecret are skipped because '' and null are falsy, so the key stays '' or null
hasKey = key instanceof Buffer ? key.length : !!key evaluates to false
Guard hasKey && !signature does not fire
Guard !hasKey && signature does not fire because the signature is empty
validateAlgorithmAndSignature runs; HS256 passes the allowlist check
if (signature && !verifySignature(...)) is skipped because the signature is empty, so no MAC is computed or compared
Claim validators run on the attacker's payload and pass

finding.guards_checked: Algorithm allowlist (passes for HS256); decoder base64url and separator checks (pass on an empty trailing segment); missingKey and missingSignature guards (neither fires when key and signature are both absent); the async path is not affected because an empty key returned from a callback is rejected in prepareKeyOrSecret (verifier.js:464, crypto.js:47-48) and utils.js getAsyncKey. Precondition: verifier configured with a non-none algorithm and key '' or null (misconfiguration).

finding.claim: When the cache is enabled, a successful verification of a token without an iat claim is cached with a TTL of cacheTTL (default 600 s) and ignores exp, so an expired token is accepted until the cache entry lapses.
finding.source: Holder of a signed token that has no iat claim and a short exp
finding.sink: Cache hit in verify returns the cached payload after exp has passed

trace.note: cacheSet sets hasIat = false when payload.iat is not a number
The block that derives the TTL from nbf and exp is skipped entirely
cacheValue[2] stays 0, so it is set to maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL
Later call: cache.get returns the cached payload
min === 0 so the lower bound passes
now <= max holds for up to cacheTTL, so the cached success is returned without re-checking exp

finding.guards_checked: exp validator at verifier.js:306-322 runs only on cache miss; tokens with iat are clamped to exp (verifier.js:125-128) and are not affected. Cache is opt-in (createCache returns null by default, verifier.js:580, utils.js). Precondition: cache enabled and token lacks iat.

finding.claim: The asymmetric JWK check only inspects the key when the first character after trim() is '{' or '[', and returns false on JSON parse failure, so a public JWK with a leading non-trimmed character is treated as an HMAC secret.
finding.source: Public JWK JSON string (public by design) supplied as the verifier key, prefixed by a character that String.prototype.trim does not remove (for example U+200B)
finding.sink: performDetectPublicKeyAlgorithms / performDetectPrivateKeyAlgorithm returns HS algorithms, and the JWK text is used as the HMAC secret; attacker forges HS256 tokens

trace.note: trimmedKey = key.trim(); U+200B is not stripped
locatePem finds no PEM header, so isRawSecret is true
assertNotAsymmetricJwkJson calls isAsymmetricJwkJson
firstChar is U+200B, not '{' or '[', so the function returns false
Alternatively, a JWK that fails JSON.parse also returns false here
Raw-secret path returns 'HS256', and prepareKeyOrSecret treats the JWK bytes as an HMAC secret

finding.guards_checked: locatePem PEM search (crypto.js:123-131) handles leading junk for PEM but not JWK; the JWK check requires position 0 after trim. Contrived precondition: key text must begin with an untrimmed invisible character or be non-parsable JSON, and the verifier must permit HS algorithms. Rated low.

finding.claim: Buffer tokens crash with a TypeError when caching is enabled, because hashToken calls String.prototype.split on a Buffer.
finding.source: Caller passes a Buffer token to verify()
finding.sink: cacheKeyBuilder(token) in hashToken throws TypeError instead of returning a TokenError

trace.note: Buffer tokens are accepted by the type check
With cache enabled, cacheKeyBuilder(token) is called with the raw Buffer
token.split('.', 1) is undefined on Buffer, so a TypeError is thrown
The same call in cacheSet would throw on the error-caching path

finding.guards_checked: Type check at verifier.js:353 accepts Buffer; the default cache is disabled so the path is only reached with cache enabled. Impact is an error-path bug with low security relevance, since remote clients normally send strings.
